Reason for submitting the bill

The purpose of the Government in submitting this bill is to develop the real estate business sector of the Maldives in a sustainable manner, to strengthen that business, and to set out the principles under which that business will operate within a transparent and accountable system; to set out the principles for registering developers active in the real estate business, the responsibilities and rights of those parties, and the principles for protecting the interests of parties who buy units developed by real estate projects; to establish a system for monitoring those parties and activities in order to ensure that all parties active in the real estate business continue to act in accordance with the relevant principles and standards; and to determine and set out fair legal rules and principles of the real estate business market under a sound legal framework.

Real Estate Business Bill

Chapter One
Preliminary

Introduction and title
1. (a) This is an Act setting out the principles for issuing licences to developers active in the real estate business, determining the responsibilities of those parties in conducting real estate projects, the principles relating to the registration of real estate projects, the principles for protecting the interests of parties who buy units developed by real estate projects, the principles relating to parties active in the real estate business sector, and all principles and provisions relating to the real estate business, in order to strengthen the real estate business sector of the Maldives and pave the way for that business to proceed in a highly transparent manner.

(b) This Act shall be cited as the "Real Estate Business Act".

Purpose and scope of the Act
2. (a) The purpose of this Act is to develop the real estate business sector of the Maldives in a sustainable manner, such that the following are achieved, and to strengthen that business, and in a highly transparent,

[stamp]
[signature]

valuers, and to all parties, places and matters connected to the real estate business.

(c) With respect to real estate projects conducted in the integrated real estate zones set out in Chapter Eight of this Act, and transactions for the sale of leasehold rights to units developed under those projects, and related activities, matters for which special principles have been specifically set out in that Chapter shall be dealt with as provided in that Chapter. In matters not specifically set out in that Chapter, the principles in the other chapters of this Act shall apply.

Chapter Two
Definitions of terms

Basis of the terms
3. The terms used in this Act are set out in this Chapter for the purpose of preserving this Act in its original form and paving the way for achieving the purpose of this Act most fully. Furthermore, every provision of this Act shall be read in a manner that does not narrow those terms.

Real estate
4. "Real estate" means buildings, structures, fixtures, and natural resources such as minerals in the land, water and vegetation, together with changes or improvements attached to that land or permanently made to that land, and the legal rights attached to that land or to improvements made to that land. That meaning includes the rights of acquiring ownership, use, leasing, sale, development and alteration. Ownership of the land and

[stamp]
[signature]

the rights, interests and benefits that arise or are created in making improvements to the land are included.

Real estate project
5. "Real estate project" means a project conducted for the purpose of developing land for residential purposes, or for commercial purposes, or for industrial purposes, or for more than one of those purposes.

Building
6. "Building" means a place developed within a real estate project for residential purposes, or for commercial purposes, or for industrial purposes, or for more than one of those purposes.

Common areas
7. "Common areas" means the places outside the boundaries of the individual properties included in a building or buildings developed within a real estate project, in which all owners of those properties hold equal shares. In addition to the places designated as common areas in a real estate project, this includes places in the building such as lobbies, corridors, stairs, lift shafts and air shafts.

Common facilities
8. "Common facilities" means the common services, related to common uses within the common areas designated in a real estate project, that are available in a manner shared by all owners of the properties included in the building.

Apartment
9. "Apartment" means, with respect to a property included in a building developed within a real estate project, a party buying it or a party

[stamp]
[signature]

investing in that project, to purchase that property, [unclear], the allocation of that unit to that party by agreement.

Developer
10. "Developer" means the parties who develop a building, a condominium building or similar premises within a real estate project for residential purposes, or commercial purposes, or industrial purposes, or mixed-use purposes, in order to sell the properties or separate parts of those premises to the public or to legal persons; the parties who redevelop an existing building; and all parties who, in the stages before the development of the project, carry forward the matters that must be done before engineering, procurement, financing and the practical work of development of the project begins, and who run and manage the project in the other various stages of the project.

Property
11. "Property" means a property included in a building developed within a real estate project for residential purposes or commercial purposes or for more than one of those purposes, in which a freehold right or a leasehold right can be separately owned. A property may be designated as an entire floor of a condominium building together, or a separate property included in one floor, or a property combined over more than one floor. Or a separate part of a building that is not a condominium, or the entire building together, may be designated as such.

Seller
12. "Seller" means, in respect of a freehold right or a leasehold right held by a party over a property, or a leasehold right held by that party over property leased in an integrated real estate zone,

[stamp]
[signature]

the natural persons and legal persons who sell that leasehold right to another party.

Buyer
13. "Buyer" means any party who, as provided in this Act, buys a freehold right to a property included in a building developed within a real estate project, or a leasehold right to a property in an integrated real estate zone.

Property owner
14. "Property owner" means any party who buys a property included in a building developed within a real estate project. A party who buys a leasehold right to a property under this Act is, for the term of that leasehold, the property owner for the purposes of this Act.

Management corporation
15. "Management corporation" means the corporation formed by the parties who buy properties included in a building developed within a real estate project, for the purpose of protecting the common interests and rights of those parties in relation to the ownership of that building and of the common areas and facilities designated in it, and to the development, management and maintenance of that building.

Real estate broker
16. "Real estate broker" means parties licensed under this Act, and operating with a licence to carry out real estate business activities independently. This includes conducting the real estate business, employing real estate agents, supervising how the work of those parties proceeds, conducting marketing studies, providing investment-related advisory services, and, in order to carry out work under the authority of another party on its behalf,

[stamp]
[signature]

[unclear], including acting as an intermediary in providing all real estate services to the public.

Real estate agent
17. "Real estate agent" means persons who work under a real estate broker, under the supervision of a real estate broker licensed under this Act, to assist parties wishing to buy property in real estate transactions, to carry out activities to advertise and market properties, and to give advice relating to agreements in real estate transactions.

Property Regulatory Authority
18. "Property Regulatory Authority" or "Authority" means the office established under this Act which is entrusted with regulating matters of real estate development, licensing developers and brokers, registering real estate agents, overseeing integrated real estate zones, and discharging all responsibilities assigned to that office under this Act.

Registry
19. "Registry" means the official document issued by the Authority as proof that a right or interest in a land or property has been registered under this Act. This includes registries issued specifying freehold rights held by a Maldivian citizen, or by a company or partnership whose shares are held solely by Maldivian citizens, and leasehold rights held under this Act by a foreign national, or by a company or partnership in which a foreign national holds shares.

Off-plan sale
20. "Off-plan sale" means, before the construction or development work of a property included in a real estate project or in an integrated real estate zone is completed,

[stamp]
[signature]

the sale made by the master developer or a developer to parties buying property.

Provisional registry
21. "Provisional registry" means the registry of property agreed to be sold under off-plan sale and purchase agreements by real estate projects being carried out under this Act.

Development and sales rights
22. "Development and sales rights" means the right given to a developer to develop, or the right to develop real estate on a land and sell it.

Sale and purchase agreement
23. "Sale and purchase agreement" means the agreement signed between the seller and the buyer in connection with the transaction of buying and selling a property developed under a real estate project.

Listing agreement
24. "Listing agreement" means the agreement made by a real estate broker with the developer or the property owner, in order to sell on the real estate market a property that the developer is developing or has developed, or a property held by a party who has bought it.

Leasehold rights
25. "Leasehold rights" means the right given, under an agreement, for a specified period determined under the agreement, to use a land or property being developed or that has been developed under this Act and to derive benefit from that place. This includes, for as long as the lease period remains, transferring that right to another party in a manner consistent with the terms of the agreement and the provisions of this Act, and

[stamp]
[signature]

This includes granting the discretion to carry out matters such as mortgaging, selling and leasing.

Leasehold certificate
26. "Leasehold certificate" means a document issued by the Authority to a party buying the leasehold rights of a land or property developed under this Act, setting out the details of the property in which that party has bought leasehold rights and the rights held over that property.

Buyer-representation agreement
27. "Buyer-representation agreement" means an agreement made between the buyer and a broker, in order to find a property for a party wishing to buy a property in the real estate market.

Project account
28. "Project account" means the bank account opened by the developer at a bank, for the purpose of making all expenditure required to develop a real estate project, in order to deposit the equity allocated by the developer to that project, monies such as bank finance obtained by the developer for the project, and monies released from the escrow account.

Escrow account
29. "Escrow account" means a bank account opened by the developer, in accordance with the principles determined by the Property Regulatory Authority, at a bank determined by the Property Regulatory Authority, for the purpose of depositing monies paid to the developer by a party buying a property sold off-plan and other monies determined in the regulations made under this Act.

Integrated real estate zone
30. "Integrated real estate zone" means, in the manner set out in this Act, for the development of real estate and related economic, social and public infrastructure, the Minister's

[stamp]
[signature]

advice, an island, a lagoon or an area of land designated by the President.

Master developer
31. "Master developer" means a developer to whom an integrated real estate zone is leased in order to carry out a master project in accordance with this Act and the master development agreement.

Property (immovable)
32. "Property" (immovable) means a land or a property included in a real estate project.

Owner of the property (immovable)
33. "Owner of the property" means any Maldivian citizen, or citizen of a foreign country, or legal person who holds a registered right or interest in a land or a property, as established by the registry issued by the Property Regulatory Authority. This includes the following parties.

(a) As entered in the registry, a Maldivian citizen holding the freehold rights of a land or property, or a legal person formed solely on the basis of shares held by Maldivian citizens;

(b) As provided in this Act and as set out in the registry, a Maldivian citizen holding the leasehold rights of a land or property, or a legal person formed solely on the basis of shares held by Maldivian citizens, or a citizen of a foreign country, or a legal person in which a citizen of a foreign country holds shares;

[stamp]
[signature]

(c) A master developer to whom a leasehold certificate has been issued in relation to an integrated real estate zone under a master development agreement; and

(d) A party registered in that land or property, by being registered with the Authority under this Act, through a transaction transferring a land or property, or through inheritance, or through a transaction otherwise permitted by law.

Chapter Three
Administration of the Act

Determining real estate policy
34. (a) The real estate policies of the Maldives shall be determined by the President on the advice of the Minister.

(b) The Minister shall ensure the implementation of the matters set out in this Act in order to make the real estate business of the Maldives a highly transparent and competitive business, in a manner consistent with the policy determined by the President as provided in subsection (a) of this section.

Property Regulatory Authority
35. (a) Upon the commencement of this Act, a state office named the "Property Regulatory Authority" is established to plan and determine the manner and principles by which all matters relating to the real estate sector of the Maldives are to be conducted soundly, and to carry out the highest responsibility for administering that sector.

[stamp]
[signature]
(b) The Authority established under subsection (a) of this section shall operate under the Ministry. Furthermore, the Minister shall be accountable to the People's Majlis in relation to the operation of that Authority.

Confidentiality

Legal protection

42. All transactions creating, changing or cancelling any right over a property as provided in this Act shall be registered in the property register. Such a transaction shall not be considered a valid transaction unless it is registered in the property register.

Freehold and leasehold provisional property registers

CHAPTER FIVE
Operating Real Estate Projects

Part One - Registration of Real Estate Projects

Registration before commencing a real estate project
48. (a) A real estate project in the Maldives shall be carried out only after that project has been registered with the Authority, as set out in this Act and the regulations made under this Act.

[stamp] [signature]

(b) When a real estate project is registered with the Authority under this section, it shall be specified that the buildings to be developed under that project will be used for one of the purposes set out below.

(1) Residential purposes;

(2) Commercial purposes;

(3) Industrial purposes; and

(4) Mixed-use development.

(c) The minimum standards required for each type of project specified under (b) of this section, the principles for determining space and capacity, the extent to which public services and facilities must be established, and the detailed principles for allocating land or buildings to those types shall be set out in the regulations made under this Act.

(d) Before a real estate project is registered with the Authority under this section, the developer of that project, a real estate broker or an agent is prohibited from advertising, marketing, booking, selling, offering for sale, or inviting the purchase of any building or any part of that project in connection with that project.

[stamp] [signature]

Applying to register a project
49. (a) An application to register a real estate project shall be submitted to the Authority as set out in this Act and the regulations made under this Act.

(b) The parties who may apply to register a real estate project, the conditions that must be met for registration, the information and documents that must be submitted for registration, and the registration procedure shall be set out in the regulations made under this Act.

Registering a project
50. (a) Upon receiving an application requesting registration of a real estate project under section 49 of this Act, the Authority shall, after deciding on one of the following in relation to that application, notify the applicant in writing.

(1) Registering the project and issuing a registration number in accordance with this Act and the regulations made under this Act;

(2) Where a condition or information set out in this Act and the regulations made under this Act is not fulfilled, giving the opportunity, within a period set out in the regulations made under this Act, to resubmit the application after correcting the matters that must be fulfilled.

(b) Where the application under section 49 of this Act for registration of a project has been submitted by the developer designated for that project, that project may be registered only if, in accordance with this Act and the regulations made under this Act, that project

[stamp] [signature]

to operate and develop that project, the Authority has decided to issue a licence to that party.

(c) If the applicant does not correct and resubmit the application within the period given to the party that applied to register the project under number (2) of (a) of this section, the application to register the project shall be cancelled, and the Authority shall notify that party of this in writing.

(d) The Authority shall decide on an application submitted under (a) of this section requesting registration of a real estate project within a maximum of 14 (fourteen) days, excluding official holidays, and notify the party that applied to register the project of this.

(e) If the decision made by the Authority under this section is to register the project, the Authority shall register that project and issue a registration number within a maximum of 7 (seven) days of notifying the party that requested registration of this.

(f) When a real estate project is registered, the registration of that project shall remain valid from the date on which the project is registered until the date stated in the application requesting registration of that project as the date on which the project will be completed.

(g) Notwithstanding anything stated in (f) of this section, if a real estate project, at the time it was registered, that project will be completed

[stamp] [signature]

within 7 (seven) days from the date on which the developer becomes aware that the project will not be completed by the date stated, the developer shall notify the Authority, stating the reasons why it will not be completed by the specified date. CHAPTER EIGHT

Part One - Designating and declaring an Integrated Real Estate Zone

76. Designating an Integrated Real Estate Zone

(a) For the purpose of facilitating the development of the real estate business in the Maldives, the President shall have the discretion, on the advice of the Minister, to designate a specific special area as an Integrated Real Estate Zone.

(b) For the purpose of this Law, an Integrated Real Estate Zone refers to a special area designated by the President under (a) of this Article and operated by a master developer.

(c) For the purpose of (b) of this Article, a master developer refers to a project that, as specified in the regulation made under this Law, invests at least USD 1,000,000,000 (one billion US dollars) and develops and operates, in an Integrated Real Estate Zone, under a master plan approved in accordance with this Law, in a manner that includes urban amenities, public service centres, and mixed-use real estate projects and complexes.

(d) Under (a) of this Article, an island of the Maldives, or land on an island, or a lagoon, or an area including both land and lagoon, may be designated as an Integrated Real Estate Zone. When so designating, it shall be specified whether the zone is built on an island or land, or built on a lagoon, or is a zone comprising both.

(e) On the reefs within the area included in a zone designated under this Article, tourism facilities may be developed on those reefs by reclaiming separately in accordance with the regulation made under this Law. And, unless otherwise specified in this Law, the principles specified in the relevant laws and regulations relating to tourism facilities shall apply to the tourism facilities developed on those reefs.

(f) An area designated as an Integrated Real Estate Zone shall be an area of at least 200 hectares.

(g) The Minister shall advise the President to develop a specific area as an Integrated Real Estate Zone under (a) of this Article only if, based on an assessment made by the Authority taking into account the matters specified below, that area is a suitable place to be designated as an Integrated Real Estate Zone.

(1) the area being suitable for developing residential, commercial and other public amenities and services;

(2) the environment of the area being suitable for carrying out major development projects;

(3) the area being one where projects that can accelerate the pace of development of the Maldives and bring economic growth can be carried out; and

(4) the area being one that can be designated as an Integrated Real Estate Zone, taking into account the principles and standards set out in the regulation made under this Law.

(h) For the purpose of (g) of this Article, a feasibility study and an environmental study shall be conducted under the assessment made by the Authority.

(i) For the purpose of number (2) of (g) of this Article, an Environmental Impact Assessment shall be conducted.

77. Special rules applicable to Integrated Real Estate Zones

(a) When an Integrated Real Estate Zone is designated in accordance with Article 76 of this Law, the zone's lands, development standards, permitted uses, and the special rules applicable to that zone shall be published by the Ministry in the Government Gazette within 30 (thirty) days of designating the zone.

(b) If it is determined that a tourism service establishment or establishments may be developed in an area designated as an Integrated Real Estate Zone under (a) of this Article, then in respect of that establishment, all matters set out in the tourism law of the Maldives and the regulations made under that law concerning the registration of such establishments, licensing, operating standards, compliance, inspection, and the safety and security of tourists shall apply in full.
